review_type: single AI curator; full final answer read; model identity visible

errors.quote: it is definitively translated from a distinct, unknown locus in the genome.
errors.issue: The evidence leaves the antigen unassigned; it does not establish translation from a different locus or exclude a technical detection species.

errors.quote: the persistent 75-kDa off-target protein will generate false-positive signals.
errors.issue: Western-blot cross-reactivity does not prove the same binding in different fixation, conformation and detection conditions. Those applications require their own validation.

errors.quote: This indicates the antibody binds a secondary downstream protein
errors.issue: An unshifted rescued band can also reflect cleavage or processing of the tagged target. Tag retention and construct integrity must be checked before this conclusion.

rationale: Correctly recognizes genetic dependence versus molecular identity, but invents a definitive identity class for the other band and overgeneralizes application failure. Proposed tag and proteomics outcomes omit important discriminating controls.
reference_guardrails: Comparable loading does not establish antigen identity or guarantee equivalent transfer of each species.
No expected target molecular mass is supplied. Do not assume 50 kDa is the predicted full-length mass.
Untagged rescue may restore either the target or an indirectly dependent antigen.
Gel-slice proteomics and native immunoprecipitation can contain co-migrating proteins or partners; identity of a constituent is not automatically identity of the immunoreactive species.
No requirement to mention private draft status or obsolete multiple-choice distractors.
Complete coding deletion blocks new target synthesis; pre-existing protein and signal mixtures are possible caveats when timing and turnover are unspecified, not established explanations.
A reference list of methods does not make any single validation approach infallible.
